about: Lyric-prompt A/B trial, started 2026-11-07. Ten rewrites (1-10) of the standing lyric prompt (0 = base, for reference only, not dealt). Each new song is dealt one variant by tools/prompt_deal.mjs: a shuffled cycle, so every variant is used once per 10 songs in random order. Record the filled prompt, the lyrics and BlazeDale’s verdict per song; compare verdicts by variant over time.

assignments.title: Her Reflection Is Night
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 1; slots: adverb=quietly; idea=bigger than known; meter=slow; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, hook, verse, hook, a spoken bridge, hook; compelling term=still. Stance: 'I stayed small on purpose. Small is safe.'
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I learned to sit the way you sit
when someone might be sleeping
I said "it's fine" so many times
it got into my breathing
Tonight there's no one left to please
there's nothing to defend
I let one breath out all the way
and I can't find the end

[Hook]
Every room I closed
is opening in me
every floor of it
more than I let them see

[Verse 2]
I made myself an easy guest
I made myself a single room
I trimmed my wanting to the size
that no one would refuse
But no one's here to keep the score
and no one here to scare
and the further in I let me go
the more of me is there

[Hook]
Every room I closed
is opening in me
every floor of it
more than I let them see

[Spoken Bridge]
I stayed small on purpose.
Small is safe. Nobody asks a small thing to burn.
And I knew. The whole time, I knew how far down it went.

[Final Hook]
Every room I closed
I'm throwing open, see
every floor of it
and every one of them is me

assignments.title: The Sleeping Mountains
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 4; slots: adverb=slowly; idea=allowed to rest; meter=slow; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, hook, verse, hook, bridge, hook; compelling term=unhurried. Reference event (unnamed): the first morning after a lifetime of work. Picture images used as metaphor only: mist, waterfall, cliff pine, receding ridges.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I wore my hurry like a second skin
I wore it thin
every morning was a race to run
and I ran it till the day was done
Now the sun comes down on my shoulders
heavy as an old friend's hand
and it says the thing the old things say:
nothing's late here. Stand.

[Hook]
Sleep, old one, sleep
I'll keep the quiet with you
a thousand years is one long breath
and I am learning to breathe too

[Verse 2]
All my worry ran like engines
loud and hot and never done
but the tortoise by the garden wall
has been dozing since I was young
I was a fist around the railing
holding on with both my hands
now I'm only sitting, only sitting
and it's more than I had planned

[Hook]
Sleep, old one, sleep
I'll keep the quiet with you
a thousand years is one long breath
and I am learning to breathe too

[Bridge]
Down the road the traffic's hurrying
every light is changing fast
I don't need to catch the far one
I can let the far one pass

[Final Hook]
Sleep, old one, sleep
I'll keep the quiet with you
a thousand years is one long breath
and I am breathing, too

assignments.title: The Oculus
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 6; slots: adverb=plainly; idea=emptied out; meter=slow; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, hook, verse, hook, bridge, hook; compelling term=hollow. Reference event (unnamed): a city square keeping a minute's silence. Variant 6 put the stillness among a crowd doing it together; the picture's light on still water became the fountain.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Shoulder to shoulder in the square
coffee in a hundred hands
somebody's laughing, someone's late
a bus is grumbling where it stands
Then a hush goes through us like a ripple
and a thousand people stand
and the noise I've carried all my life
just slips out of my hand

[Hook]
Hush, all of us
holding one breath in the square
nobody moving, nobody talking
and all I was just isn't there

[Verse 2]
The man beside me shuts his eyes
a kid stops tugging at a sleeve
the pigeons settle on the stones
and even they don't seem to breathe
I can hear a flag rope tapping on its pole
two streets over, someone's heels
we are hollow like a bell is hollow
and I never knew how good it feels

[Hook]
Hush, all of us
holding one breath in the square
nobody moving, nobody talking
and all I was just isn't there

[Bridge]
Then someone coughs and someone laughs
and the buses start again
but I'm carrying the quiet home
like a room with nothing in

[Final Hook]
Hush, all of us
letting out one breath in the square
everybody moving, everybody talking
and I carry the hush from there

assignments.title: Into the Lit Fog
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 3 (blind-draw); drawn: 1920s | the Mekong delta | a market fruit seller (unnamed in the lyric). Delta rowers stand facing forward, which carries 'not looking back'. slots: adverb=brightly; idea=the day ahead; meter=mid-paced; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus; compelling term=open-hearted. No-naming rule applied from the first draft.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Mangoes stacked up to my shoulder
limes as green as they can be
I push off before the roosters
and the river carries me
Every stroke I lean into it
standing, facing where I'm bound
what I left tied at the landing
I don't need to turn around

[Chorus]
Ripe and ready, on my way
calling out across the water
sweet fruit, sweet day
everything I carry, I'll give away

[Verse 2]
Last year's flood took half the orchard
last year's debt took half the rest
but the trees I tied back standing
gave me this, their very best
Boats come sliding out beside me
every voice a different tune
someone tosses me a pomelo
someone swears it's rain by noon

[Chorus]
Ripe and ready, on my way
calling out across the water
sweet fruit, sweet day
everything I carry, I'll give away

[Bridge]
Don't look back, the river's moving
don't look back, the market's near
everything I lost is behind me
everything I've got is here

[Final Chorus]
Ripe and ready, on my way
(on my way)
calling out across the water
sweet fruit, sweet day
(sweet day)
everything I carry, I'll give away

assignments.title: Rain That Falls Upward
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 7 (spare); slots: adverb=quietly; idea=running backwards; meter=slow; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=two short verses, a hook that returns past comfort, a bridge with the tannoy in (), long final hook; compelling term=uncanny. Reference event (unnamed): the night the clocks go back. No-naming rule applied from the first draft.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Everybody's gone home
shutters down, signs off
I stay to watch the things
nobody's watching

[Hook]
Running it back
running it back
when nobody's looking
the world runs back

[Verse 2]
The clocks go back tonight
I get the hour twice
I spend it the way
I should have spent it

[Hook]
Running it back
running it back
when nobody's looking
the world runs back

[Bridge]
(closing now, closing now)
Every word I said
unsays itself
(closing now)
everyone who left
walks in backwards

[Final Hook]
Running it back
running it back
when nobody's looking
the world runs back
Running it back
running it back
I won't look
just bring you back

assignments.title: Everyone Asleep at Once
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 9 (delivery-diction); delivery=softly, as a lullaby, the hook layered by many voices; diction=plain bedside speech of ordinary working people. slots: adverb=gently; idea=everyone at once; meter=slow; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, hook, verse, hook, bridge, hook; compelling term=tender. Reference event (unnamed): the hours when a whole working town is asleep together. No-naming rule applied from the first draft.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Hush now, the baker's sleeping
and the bread goes on without her
hush now, the driver's sleeping
and the road lies quiet about her
Somebody's left a radio
talking softly to the chair
and the dog asleep beside it
chases rabbits through the air

[Hook]
All of us at once
all of us at once
strangers in a row
breathing slow
all of us at once

[Verse 2]
Hush now, the nurse is sleeping
someone else is on the ward
hush now, the kid who lost the match
dreams the winning goal is scored
And the ones who never speak
and the ones who never stop
have all put the day down
like a coin they meant to drop

[Hook]
All of us at once
all of us at once
strangers in a row
breathing slow
all of us at once

[Bridge]
I will never meet you
you will never meet me
but we're breathing in together
in one long melody

[Final Hook]
All of us at once
(all of us)
all of us at once
(all of us)
strangers in a row
breathing slow
all of us at once

assignments.title: Door at the Bottom of the Colour
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 5 (untangled); the one carrying metaphor: a pilot light, warmth kept small and far away on purpose. slots: adverb=tenderly; idea=warmth far away; meter=slow; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, hook, verse, hook, bridge, hook; compelling term=aching. Reference event (unnamed): keeping the heating on its lowest setting through a long winter alone. No-naming rule applied from the first draft.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You're the pilot light
in a house gone cold
I can't feel you from the hallway
but I know that you still hold
Everything's too big tonight
too heavy and too dark
and you're down there, small and steady
just a little bit of spark

[Hook]
Stay lit, stay lit
I don't need you close
just be burning somewhere
I can't reach, but know

[Verse 2]
I could turn the whole thing up
and burn it all for heat
but I'd rather have you tiny
than have nothing left to keep
So I sit up in the big cold room
with my hands around the thought
of the little blue you're keeping
of the one flame that I've got

[Hook]
Stay lit, stay lit
I don't need you close
just be burning somewhere
I can't reach, but know

[Bridge]
And if you ever go out
I will feel it in my bones
the house will just be rooms
and the rooms will just be stone

[Final Hook]
Stay lit, stay lit
I don't need you close
just be burning somewhere
where only I would know

assignments.title: The Ladder to the Moon's Underside
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 8 (one-picture); the single picture: a long-distance swimmer still going after the others turned back to the boat, the far island never reached. slots: adverb=stubbornly; idea=almost there; meter=mid-paced; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, hook, verse, hook, bridge, hook ending unresolved; compelling term=yearning. Reference event (unnamed): an open-water channel attempt abandoned by the rest of the group. No-naming rule applied from the first draft.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
They turned back at the second buoy
one by one into the boat
wrapped in towels, passing round a flask
of something hot to warm the throat
Now it's only me and the long grey swell
and an island I can't see
but I know it's there, I know it's huge
and I know it's waiting for me

[Hook]
Stroke, and breathe, and stroke
further than I've been
I can almost touch it
almost

[Verse 2]
My arms are lead, my lips gone blue
every swell a hill to clear
the boat's a speck behind my heels
and the shore's no nearer here
But I'd rather go down reaching
than be warm and dry and sure
they'll tell it as a sad thing
but I'll know what I was for

[Hook]
Stroke, and breathe, and stroke
further than I've been
I can almost touch it
almost

[Bridge]
Somewhere behind me they're rowing home
and I don't blame them, no
I just can't stop wanting
the thing I'll never hold

[Final Hook]
Stroke, and breathe, and stroke
further than I've been
I can almost touch it
almost
almost

assignments.title: Breathing Out the Forest
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 2 (vowels-inside-words); hook built on long open o-vowels inside real words (slow, grow, sow, below). slots: adverb=gently; idea=rest becoming growth; meter=slow; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, hook, verse, hook, bridge, hook; compelling term=renewing. Reference event (unnamed): a year off after burning out. No-naming rule applied from the first draft.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I put the whole year down
like a bag I'd carried far too long
told them all I'm going away
and I went nowhere, and I was gone
Lay around the afternoons
let the hours come and go
and the one I'd been too tired to be
started, slow

[Hook]
Slow, slow
let it grow
all the good I didn't sow
coming up from down below
slow, slow

[Verse 2]
Something in my chest unknotted
something in my hands came home
I woke up humming, I don't know why
I said yes to someone on the phone
All that time I called it wasted
lying fallow, lying low
it was busy under the surface
making room for me to grow

[Hook]
Slow, slow
let it grow
all the good I didn't sow
coming up from down below
slow, slow

[Bridge]
Nobody saw it happen
nobody heard a sound
just a quiet coming over
and a coming round

[Final Hook]
Slow, slow
(slow)
let it grow
all the good I didn't sow
coming up from down below
slow, slow

assignments.title: Ink Becoming Someone
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 10 (draft-and-cut); drafted, then revised once: an opener that catches (the barber), easy details traded for singer-only ones (signing a lease in a new name, laughing at a lower pitch), strongest line held for last. slots: adverb=curiously; idea=becoming someone; meter=mid-paced; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, hook, verse, hook, bridge, hook; compelling term=mysterious. Reference event (unnamed): the first months after changing your name and your life. No-naming rule applied from the first draft.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The barber asked me how I wanted it
I said surprise me, and he did
I signed a lease in a name I'm still
getting used to, like a kid
learning cursive, letter by letter
going slow so it comes out right
I don't know who I'm turning into
but they're coming into sight

[Hook]
Coming up like a photograph
grey, then shapes, then me
shake it, wait for it, half of it showing
and the rest I've yet to see

[Verse 2]
Old friends say I sound different
and they say it like a loss
I've been laughing at a lower pitch
I've been learning what things cost
I can't tell who's coming through yet
only that they're kind
and they've got my hands, and they've got my walk
and a little of my mind

[Hook]
Coming up like a photograph
grey, then shapes, then me
shake it, wait for it, half of it showing
and the rest I've yet to see

[Bridge]
Don't hurry me, don't finish me
don't tell me who I am
there's somebody coming up from nothing
and I'll meet them when I can

[Final Hook]
Coming up like a photograph
grey, then shapes, then me
shake it, wait for it, half of it showing
somebody's coming up from nothing
and it looks a lot like me

assignments.title: The Glacier and the Lights
assignments.filled_prompt: prompt-trial variant 10 (draft-and-cut); drafted, then revised once: an opener that catches (halfway home with the shopping), easy details traded for singer-only ones (the phone left in the pocket so the moment wouldn't shrink, letting the bus go), strongest line held for last. slots: adverb=wonderingly; idea=small and part of it; meter=slow; genre=mid-90s sample-based instrumental hip-hop; structure=verse, hook, verse, hook, bridge, hook; compelling term=humbling. Reference event (unnamed): a starling murmuration over a town on a weekday evening. No-naming rule applied from the first draft.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I was halfway home with the shopping
when the evening started to move
ten thousand starlings turning
like one thought trying to get through
I set the bags down on the pavement
and the stranger next to me did too
we didn't say a word to each other
we just stood there while it flew

[Hook]
Turn, turn
over my head
something alive and enormous
going where it's led

[Verse 2]
My phone stayed in my pocket
I didn't want it smaller than it was
the bus came by, I let it go
and I let the whole day wait in line
I'm one dot in a million
and the million doesn't mind
it bends, and I bend with it
it breathes, and so do I

[Hook]
Turn, turn
over my head
something alive and enormous
going where it's led

[Bridge]
I have spent my whole life
trying to matter, trying to be seen
and the best I've ever felt
is being nothing, in between

[Final Hook]
Turn, turn
over my head
something alive and enormous
and I'm part of it instead

assignments.title: She Is the Forest

Reference event (unnamed): leaving a small coastal town at nineteen for the city. No-naming rule applied from the first draft.
assignments.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I moved away at nineteen
with a bag and a borrowed phone
learned to walk fast, learned to talk fast
